denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 35301 (carotid endarterectomy) with date of service 2026-04-12. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish the degree of stenosis or the symptomatic status required for coverage.

criteria.text: Symptomatic carotid stenosis: transient ischemic attack, amaurosis fugax, or non-disabling stroke in the ipsilateral territory within the past 6 months with 50 to 99 percent stenosis; or asymptomatic 70 to 99 percent stenosis with a life expectancy over 5 years and a perioperative stroke and death risk under 3 percent.
Degree of stenosis documented by duplex ultrasound using velocity criteria, confirmed by CT or MR angiography when indicated, reported by the NASCET method.
Best medical therapy in place: antiplatelet therapy and a high-intensity statin.
Surgery planned within 14 days of the index event when feasible.

chart.text: Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Vitamin D came back 15. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Here with a cough and congestion for 5 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
A1c came back 6.8. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Mole on the upper back that his spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.

Twenty minutes of right arm weakness and slurred speech that resolved before arrival. CT head without hemorrhage or infarct. ABCD2 score 5. Aspirin given, carotid imaging ordered, neurology consulted.

81 year old man in vascular surgery clinic after a recent neurologic event, sent by neurology. Significant plaque on the left. Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary disease with a remote stent. Discussed endarterectomy versus stenting; endarterectomy preferred for this anatomy and age. His history otherwise: osteoarthritis of the hands. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives with his spouse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Transient ischemic attack 3 days ago, right arm and face, now back to baseline. Symptomatic left carotid disease. Aspirin 81 and clopidogrel 75 started in the emergency department, atorvastatin 80 nightly, blood pressure 138 over 82 today. Scheduling endarterectomy within 2 weeks of the event per guideline; the operating room is booked for 8 days from today.

Returned with his spouse to go over the operation, the risk of stroke with and without surgery, cranial nerve injury, and the hospital stay of one night. Wants to proceed. Vitals today 127 over 78, pulse 66.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Blood pressure check. 137 over 81 today, 122 over 83 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Pre-op. Anesthesia evaluation done, EKG unchanged. Continue aspirin and clopidogrel through surgery. Consent signed.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-2 (imaging); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
